copies.headline: Noah's Backfield Brings a Knife to Tampa
copies.body:
This is decided in the backfield, where Adam is up 43 to 28 on the top two. Kenneth Walker III carries a questionable tag, but even if he sits, Bucky Irving gets Carolina at home in a 43.5-total game Tampa is favored in, and Rico Dowdle and Kenny Gainwell are real insurance. Noah's answer is James Cook III against Kansas City and Rhamondre Stevenson in a 35.5-total slog at the Chargers — the lowest number on the board. That's not a committee, that's a hostage situation.
Receiver compounds it: 47 to 34 for Adam, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba in a 46.5-total divisional game and Chris Olave chasing a 10-point deficit in Cincinnati, where New Orleans will throw it 45 times. Noah's edges are Jayden Daniels (+4) and a questionable Sam LaPorta. Adam is first in scoring, first in all-play at 67 percent; Noah is last in both and has scored 89.2 and 91.4 the past two weeks.

copies.headline: John Scores More, Logan Has Burrow
copies.body:
The quarterback gap is the whole game. Joe Burrow against New Orleans, a ten-point home favorite in a 50.5-total, is the single best asset on either roster, and John is countering with Caleb Williams at Detroit or Stafford against Green Bay in a 43.5-total that suggests grinding. That's nine projected points of daylight, and receiver widens it: Justin Jefferson, Tetairoa McMillan and Luther Burden to John's Tee Higgins and then a cliff into DeMario Douglas and Xavier Hutchinson at nine. Higgins in that Bengals shootout is real; the WR2 and WR3 slots are not.
John's counterweight is running back and tight end, and it's genuine — Kyren Williams, Jonah Coleman and D'Andre Swift versus Jaylen Warren and Zach Charbonnet, plus Trey McBride. But six at back and two at tight end don't erase twenty-one. Logan's thin spot is depth behind Burrow; if Cincinnati gets ugly early, this flips.

copies.headline: Christian Scores Like a Contender, Loses Like Isaac
copies.body:
The spread here lives at receiver. Isaac's top three — Ja'Marr Chase (26) against a Saints defense Cincinnati is favored by 10 on a 50.5, Malik Nabers, Jakobi Meyers in a Jacksonville game they're favored by 14.5 in — clear Christian's best three by eight, and that's before noting Chase is the only genuine 35-point ceiling on either side. Christian's WR room is deeper (Lamb, Smith, Jameson Williams, Deebo, Shakir) but it's a committee: six guys projected 9 to 20, none of whom singlehandedly wins a week. Lamb at least gets the Dallas-Philly 47.5 total with the Cowboys favored, so the volume's there.
Everywhere else is a coin flip. Lawrence edges Stroud by two, Kittle edges Hockenson by two, the backfields are within a point. The real risk is Isaac's: Saquon Barkley questionable as a 14-point underdog, Tuten questionable on the other side. Christian is the better team — 127.8 per game, 65% all-play, minus-2.2 in luck — and he already hung 124 on Isaac in Week 6. But Isaac's receivers are in the two best scoring environments on the slate.

copies.headline: Leif's 8-3 Finally Meets Its Receiver Problem
copies.body:
This is decided at wideout, where Grant has a nine-point edge in top-three projections and the better game environments to back it. Amon-Ra St. Brown is in Detroit-Chicago at 55.5, the week's juiciest total, and Zay Flowers gets Baltimore as a 6.5-point dog in Houston, which means volume late whether the Ravens want it or not. Leif's answer is Mike Evans at 15 and Stefon Diggs at 14, then a cliff into Courtland Sutton at 8 and a questionable Omar Cooper Jr., with Davante Adams on IR. That third receiver spot is a hole, not a flex.
Leif's edges are real but small: Josh Allen over Mahomes in the same 47.5-point game is a wash, and Christian McCaffrey plus Derrick Henry is three points on Judkins and Pollard, with Tennessee a 14.5-point dog unlikely to feed Pollard a lead. Leif's 8-3 is built on +2.6 luck wins and a 49% all-play; Grant is 5-6 with better scoring and a -0.9 luck figure. The math catches up.

copies.headline: Mitchell Is Peaking, CJ Is Coasting
copies.body:
Mitchell gives up nothing at quarterback — Dak Prescott against Philadelphia in a 47.5 total matches Deshaun Watson in a Browns-Raiders game with a 41.5 total, which is the kind of number you set your watch to for 14 fantasy points. Everywhere else it tilts. Jahmyr Gibbs alone (26 projected) nearly matches CJ's top two backs, and Detroit-Chicago at 55.5 is the highest total on the slate, with the Lions as underdogs, meaning Gibbs touches it in every situation. CJ's RB room is Chuba Hubbard in a 43.5-total road game and a Jonathan Taylor whose Colts are 6.5-point home dogs, which at least keeps the volume up. At tight end, Travis Kelce in Buffalo versus Darren Waller is a five-point hole CJ cannot plug.
The receiver gap is the quieter problem. Mitchell's top three go 45; CJ needs Parker Washington's 18 to hold in a game Jacksonville is favored by 14.5 and may simply run out. Mitchell has scored 128.6, 149.0 and 162.9 the last three weeks and sits 4th in the power rankings at 4-7 because the schedule hated him. CJ is 6-5 on +1.3 luck wins, 9th in scoring, 43% all-play, and hasn't cleared 120 since September. The Week 6 blowout was Mitchell's season low, not evidence.

copies.headline: Peter's Ceiling Finally Outruns Kaleb's Luck
copies.body:
Kaleb is 7-4 with the worst scoring average in the league, which is less a team and more a magic trick — +2.9 wins above expected, 37% all-play, and a power ranking of 10th that still flatters him. The positional edges are thin: four points at running back behind Ashton Jeanty and Breece Hall, nothing at quarterback with Goff matching Cousins on paper, and a tight end gap that goes to Peter if Brock Bowers clears his questionable tag. Kaleb's receiver room is wide but shallow — Drake London in a 42.5 total as a seven-point dog, Ladd McConkey in a 35.5-total slog, and Carnell Tate with Tennessee getting 14.5 points in Jacksonville, which at least means garbage-time volume.
Peter's path is the better game environment. George Pickens draws Dallas-Philadelphia at 47.5 with the Cowboys favored, Bijan Robinson gets Minnesota's defense but Atlanta will be throwing from behind, and Goff in a 55.5-point Detroit game is Kaleb's one real swing. The depth matters: Peter has three startable quarterbacks and three tight ends; Kaleb has Jordan Addison doubtful and RJ Harvey on IR.

intro: Grant at Leif is the one worth watching, a game between a 5-6 roster that needs it to stay alive and the 8-3 team that can't afford to hand the bye back to Adam or Kaleb, and Grant's the slimmest of favorites on the road. The widest gap is Peter over Kaleb, which is the sort of thing that happens when the 7-4 team's lineup is held together by bye-week fill-ins and a running back room nobody would start by choice. Everything from fourth down to tenth is separated by one game, so Christian, Logan, Isaac and Peter are all essentially playing elimination football three weeks early.
